title: slot-repack-savings-explorer
description: Lightweight spreadsheet + scenario explorer for ‘slot repacking’ and capacity rescue strategies. Purpose: quantify savings from intra-pool repacking, scheduled idle consolidation, and short-term buyback vs. long-run reserve commitments. Focused on committed GPU pools (NVIDIA A100/RTX) and mixed tenancy (dedicated + overflow).
executive_summary: Preliminary modelling shows that modest dynamic repacking (20% of idle capacity reclaimed weekly) can reduce blended per-GPU effective cost by ~8–15% versus static reserved allocation, depending on on-demand spot spreads and burst-window length. This sheet compares 6 candidate strategies and sensitivity to utilization and spot price volatility.
assumptions: Reserved unit price: $2.40/hr (per-GPU amortized across contract)
On-demand equivalent: $3.60/hr (cloud on-demand list price proxy)
Base peak utilization: 72% average across pool
Idle reclaim efficiency: percentage of idle GPUs that can be consolidated (range 10%–40%)
Operational repack cost: 0.5% extra engineering time + negligible token-level impact
sheet_rows: Scenario,Reserved GPUs,Avg Utilization,Idle Reclaimed %,Burst Use hrs/month,On-demand hrs/month,Blended cost ($/hr/gpu),Effective cost delta vs reserved,Months to breakeven (vs new reserve)
sensitivity_analysis: Run knobs: reserved price ±15%, spot price ±30%, reclaim efficiency ±10pp, utilization ±8pp. Key observation: when reserved price falls by 10% the marginal value of repacking drops but remains positive unless utilization exceeds 88%. If spot volatility spikes (spot > 1.6x expected), hybrid buyback loses advantage.
detailed_notes: Rows in sheet_rows are simplified aggregates — actual model includes per-region price bands, GPU sku mix (A100-40GB vs A100-80GB), and burst latency SLO costs. Repacking operationally requires fast preemption policies, KV-cache sticky mapping, and brief migration windows to avoid long tail latency. Investigate automated repack flows triggered by 3-hour moving-average idle signal, with a cooldown to avoid churning.
recommendations: 1) Pilot 'Consolidate-weekly' on a single pool for 8 weeks (monitor user-perceived latency and cache miss rate). 2) Add a small spot-buyback budget to allow short bursts while maintaining reserved baseline. 3) Build telemetry: per-slot idle histogram, repack churn counter, and cost-per-token by repack cohort. 4) Re-evaluate commit sizing guidance to customers with >200 GPUs recommending 10% slack to enable safe repacking.
open_questions: How many workloads will accept ephemeral migration without quality regression?
Can we automate eviction notice with 30s warning for cached KV warming?
What contractual language is required to guarantee repack behavior for Dedicated customers?
Is there appetite from sales to offer 'repack-enabled' lower-price SLA?
next_steps: 1) Wire-up capacity simulator (github PR referenced above) to replay last 12 months of slot-level telemetry. 2) Run A/B pilot with one committed customer pool in us-west-2. 3) Draft short customer-facing one-pager that explains repack mechanics and expected savings. 4) Sync with SRE on migration automation and with legal on contract terms.
methodology_summary: This sheet uses a blended-cost model: blended_cost = (reserved_hours * reserved_price + on_demand_hours * on_demand_price + spot_hours * spot_price) / total_effective_hours. We model idle reclaim as shifting reserved idle hours into either spot (if sold back) or used for burst. Breakeven months computed vs buying additional reserved capacity at current reserved_price and amortization assumptions.
footer_notes: Draft for internal review. Numbers are directional; do not share externally. Contact owner for raw simulator inputs and per-region breakdowns. Last updated 2025-02-18.
